output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT on matter and supervisor), then competing-hypotheses weighing, then evidence-provenance check on exit forms.
output.brief: Resignations are concentrated in the Kestrel team: 8 of 11 Kestrel associates left, against 1 of 13 other associates in the group. Other groups look normal, and the billable-target rise applied firm-wide, so neither it nor general market mobility explains this. Pay is probably not the main driver, since the Kestrel/non-Kestrel split is so lopsided, though pay may play a smaller part. I can't yet separate the heavy Kestrel workload from Dorian Faulk's supervision: all 11 Kestrel associates reported to him and he supervises no one else. The survey comments point to both. The exit forms are weak evidence because leavers knew the group head might read them. I'd advise against the £12k group-wide payment and closing the review. It would not address the concentration and would end the inquiry. Commission the confidential external interviews (about £9k, three weeks), structured to separate workload from supervision. Meanwhile, add matter and supervising partner to attrition reporting. Hold off on moving supervision or funding contract reviewers until the interviews show which cause matters. Confidence in the concentration finding is high. Confidence on supervision versus workload is low.
